code: # Everyday vocabulary -> HS code.
# code     2
# terms    Semicolon-separated words people actually type.
# primary  yes  = searching any of these terms produces the confident
#                "<term> sits in HS <code>" answer card.
#          no   = the terms only boost ranking; no answer card.
# note     One short plain sentence shown under the answer card.
# THE ORGANISING RULE
#   A generic or plural term answers at HS-4:   "batteries"  -> 8507
#   A specific product term answers at HS-6:    "lithium ion battery" -> 850760
# That is what makes the 2- and 4-digit codes first-class rather than a
# by-product of the six-digit list. When someone asks about a category they
# get the category; when they ask about a product they get the product.
# A hand-written row here always wins over the automatic rule that promotes
# a unique product label from fed_sector_definition.csv to an answer term.
# Lines starting with # are ignored. Edit freely
# `python pipeline/build_hs_library.py`.
